narrative:
The model determined that you have a 58% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the size of the loan you requested, the status of your checking account, and the level of savings you have. The large loan amount of 13,756 DM was the biggest driver pushing the decision toward denial. This amount is more than four times higher than the average requested by applicants who were approved, and the model sees such large requests as substantially increasing risk.

Your checking account status of “none” worked in your favor and was the second most important factor. Most approved applicants (59%) also have no checking account, so this is viewed as fairly normal and helped pull the prediction back toward approval.

Unfortunately, having unknown or no savings was the third strongest influence and pushed the prediction back toward bad credit risk. This is a common profile among applicants, but in combination with the very large loan size it signaled higher risk to the model.

The overall combination resulted in a prediction above the acceptable threshold. To improve your chances on a future application, consider requesting a significantly smaller loan amount that is more in line with what successful applicants typically ask for, or take time to build verifiable savings before reapplying.
